chapters.title: Chapter 4789: Egregious! III
paragraphs: The voice seemed to carry extra weight when speaking his distinction. Extra resonance. As if even the ancient gate recognized that something unprecedented was walking through its threshold.
Many Glossarians made way for him.

Their looks were those of awe and wonder. This was the being who had contributed 9 new letters to The First Tongue, as some very well knew. This was THE Glossarian. This was someone who had achieved what even Absolutes could not.
Ahead, heavy noise bustled!
Noah looked at it all.

The interior of the Arena opened before him in magnificent scope. It followed a modified amphitheater design with distinct sections arranged in concentric circles descending toward the central combat floor. Thousands upon thousands of seats filled with beings of every description.
He saw entities of the other three philosophies here.

Chaosites and Paradoxians were roaring with fervor! They cheered and shouted, their sections a cacophony of noise and movement! Some celebrated the challenge itself! Others celebrated the chaos it would bring! Their energy was infectious, spreading excitement through the crowd like wildfire!
Existentialists watched on calmly and silently.

Their section was still. Observant. They did not cheer or jeer. They simply existed, witnessing what would unfold with the patience of those who understood that all things eventually revealed their truth.
And on the very bottom of the Arena floor...
There was a dog looking around while frowning cutely!
Skoll sat in what appeared to be a Substitution Circle, his neon flames flickering with uncertainty. His massive head turned this way and that, trying to understand why he had been brought here.
Why so many beings were watching him.
Why the nice people who had been helping his Master suddenly couldn’t help him anymore.
He looked confused.
He looked worried.
But he was still a good boy, sitting patiently and waiting for his Master to come.
Noah’s eyes flashed sharply as he saw this.
He went further in.
Lunaris spoke as they descended deeper into the Arena, her pages rustling with the formal delivery of necessary information.
"Within The Palaestra of Primordial Reckoning, certain rules are absolute."
Her voice carried professional weight.
"No faction may attack another’s members outside the combat floor. This neutral ground is sacred. Violations are punished by all four Strategoi acting in unison."
They continued descending.
"Strategoi cannot directly interfere with challenges they did not issue. Glossikos the Articulate cannot intervene on your behalf, no matter how much she may wish to."
Her pages shifted uneasily.
"The Right of Challenge, once properly invoked, cannot be withdrawn. THE Weavers began this. It must be seen through to conclusion."
They passed through rings of seating.
Hoplites watched with wide eyes as Noah passed. Lochagoi nodded with respect. Polemarchs observed with calculating gazes.
Lunaris continued her explanation.
"The combat floor is called The Circle of Reckoning. It is the heart of The Palaestra."
Her pages displayed diagrams as she spoke.

"Circular, approximately 1 kilometer in diameter. The floor can expand or contract based on the nature of the battle. For Absolute-level conflicts, it extends to accommodate existential-warping combat."
They were getting closer now.

"The surface is composed of Reckoning Stone, a material that absorbs and neutralizes residual Civilizational Authority as it bears dozens of Philologies. It is inscribed with a massive seal combining elements from all four philosophies. The central point is called The Nexus of Truth. It glows faintly at all times."
She gestured toward the compass points of the Arena floor.
"The Four Pillars stand at cardinal directions around arena itself..."
Noah could see them now.

"The Pillar of Words to the North. Glossarian. It records everything said during combat. The Pillar of Contradiction to the South. Paradoxian. It displays paradoxes emerging from battle. The Pillar of Being to the East. Existentialist. It tracks the existential state of combatants. The Pillar of Entropy to the West. Chaosite. It measures chaos generated by conflict."
Her voice grew more serious.

"The Arena can generate environmental challenges based on the nature of the conflict. Barriers can be erected to contain specific types of energy as even Strategoi may not be able to leave until the battle is over, and none...can interfere."
She paused.
"In short, sir, once you step onto that floor, you cannot leave until the challenge is resolved."
Noah barely gave a glance to all the things she mentioned.
His gaze remained on Skoll.

But he was also looking around at the higher areas of the Arena. The concentric rings of countless seats had Hoplites just above the Arena floor. Then Lochagoi in the next ring up. Then Polemarchs higher still.
And far above them all...
The Strategoi Thrones floated at the highest level.
Four massive throne platforms positioned above their respective faction’s gates.
Glossikos the Articulate’s Throne hung above the North Gate. It was constructed from living pages that constantly wrote and rewrote themselves. Floating Phonemes orbited around it like satellites.
The seat itself was carved from crystallized First Tongue, each armrest inscribed with her personal Theses. Currently empty, as she was in The Mouseion on his behalf.

Paradoxos the Dual’s Throne floated above the South Gate. Two thrones fused into one, facing opposite directions yet somehow both facing the Arena. Half obsidian, half gold, the division line constantly shifting. Observers reported seeing one occupant or two depending on the angle of observation. Currently occupied by... something. Someone. It was difficult to tell. It could also be empty.

Ontikos the Unwavering’s Throne sat above the East Gate. A single block of uncarved white marble, utterly simple yet radiating profound presence. No decorations. No inscriptions. Just pure existence given form. The most stable structure in the entire Arena, unmoved by any battle below.

Khaotikos the Unbound’s Throne existed above the West Gate. Or it didn’t. The throne refused to maintain consistent form. Sometimes it appeared as a pile of debris, sometimes as an elaborate seat, sometimes as nothing at all.
As Noah watched all of this, there was no sign of THE Weavers anywhere.
The of the four thrones of Absolutes far above may or may not be occupied, but THE Weavers themselves were absent from the Arena floor.
So he simply took a step.
He appeared on the Arena floor in an instant.
Skoll turned toward him immediately!
The massive dog’s tail began wagging with enthusiasm! His neon flames brightened! His worried frown transformed into canine joy as he bounded over to his Master!
Noah rubbed his head with a smile.
"You okay, boy?"
He asked such a simple question.
And Skoll...
Woof!
Nodded affirmatively!
His tail wagged even harder. Everything was fine now. His Master was here. Whatever had been confusing and scary before no longer mattered.
Such a good boy!
And a moment later, a voice boomed out across the bustling Arena.
The noise of the crowd diminished as The Voice of Reckoning spoke.
"The challenge today has been intercepted. The Polemarch, THE Genesis Monarch, is stepping in for the challenged Hoplite."
A murmur rippled through the crowd.
"The Challenger has no qualms about this."
The Voice paused.
"They are now called to the stage."
All eyes turned toward the South Gate.
The Paradoxian entrance.
Where THE Weavers would emerge.

sentences.text: The voice seemed to carry extra weight when speaking his distinction.
Extra resonance.
As if even the ancient gate recognized that something unprecedented was walking through its threshold.
Many Glossarians made way for him.
Their looks were those of awe and wonder.
This was the being who had contributed 9 new letters to The First Tongue, as some very well knew.
This was THE Glossarian.
This was someone who had achieved what even Absolutes could not.
Ahead, heavy noise bustled!
Noah looked at it all.
The interior of the Arena opened before him in magnificent scope.
It followed a modified amphitheater design with distinct sections arranged in concentric circles descending toward the central combat floor.
Thousands upon thousands of seats filled with beings of every description.
He saw entities of the other three philosophies here.
Chaosites and Paradoxians were roaring with fervor!
They cheered and shouted, their sections a cacophony of noise and movement!
Some celebrated the challenge itself!
Others celebrated the chaos it would bring!
Their energy was infectious, spreading excitement through the crowd like wildfire!
Existentialists watched on calmly and silently.
Their section was still.
Observant.
They did not cheer or jeer.
They simply existed, witnessing what would unfold with the patience of those who understood that all things eventually revealed their truth.
And on the very bottom of the Arena floor...
There was a dog looking around while frowning cutely!
Skoll sat in what appeared to be a Substitution Circle, his neon flames flickering with uncertainty.
His massive head turned this way and that, trying to understand why he had been brought here.
Why so many beings were watching him.
Why the nice people who had been helping his Master suddenly couldn’t help him anymore.
He looked confused.
He looked worried.
But he was still a good boy, sitting patiently and waiting for his Master to come.
Noah’s eyes flashed sharply as he saw this.
He went further in.
Lunaris spoke as they descended deeper into the Arena, her pages rustling with the formal delivery of necessary information.
"Within The Palaestra of Primordial Reckoning, certain rules are absolute."
Her voice carried professional weight.
"No faction may attack another’s members outside the combat floor.
This neutral ground is sacred.
Violations are punished by all four Strategoi acting in unison."
They continued descending.
"Strategoi cannot directly interfere with challenges they did not issue.
Glossikos the Articulate cannot intervene on your behalf, no matter how much she may wish to."
Her pages shifted uneasily.
"The Right of Challenge, once properly invoked, cannot be withdrawn.
THE Weavers began this.
It must be seen through to conclusion."
They passed through rings of seating.
Hoplites watched with wide eyes as Noah passed.
Lochagoi nodded with respect.
Polemarchs observed with calculating gazes.
Lunaris continued her explanation.
"The combat floor is called The Circle of Reckoning.
It is the heart of The Palaestra."
Her pages displayed diagrams as she spoke.
"Circular, approximately 1 kilometer in diameter.
The floor can expand or contract based on the nature of the battle.
For Absolute-level conflicts, it extends to accommodate existential-warping combat."
They were getting closer now.
"The surface is composed of Reckoning Stone, a material that absorbs and neutralizes residual Civilizational Authority as it bears dozens of Philologies.
It is inscribed with a massive seal combining elements from all four philosophies.
The central point is called The Nexus of Truth.
It glows faintly at all times."
She gestured toward the compass points of the Arena floor.
"The Four Pillars stand at cardinal directions around arena itself..."
Noah could see them now.
"The Pillar of Words to the North.
Glossarian.
It records everything said during combat.
The Pillar of Contradiction to the South.
Paradoxian.
It displays paradoxes emerging from battle.
The Pillar of Being to the East.
Existentialist.
It tracks the existential state of combatants.
The Pillar of Entropy to the West.
Chaosite.
It measures chaos generated by conflict."
Her voice grew more serious.
"The Arena can generate environmental challenges based on the nature of the conflict.
Barriers can be erected to contain specific types of energy as even Strategoi may not be able to leave until the battle is over, and none...can interfere."
She paused.
"In short, sir, once you step onto that floor, you cannot leave until the challenge is resolved."

His gaze remained on Skoll.
But he was also looking around at the higher areas of the Arena.
The concentric rings of countless seats had Hoplites just above the Arena floor.
Then Lochagoi in the next ring up.
Then Polemarchs higher still.

Four massive throne platforms positioned above their respective faction’s gates.

It was constructed from living pages that constantly wrote and rewrote themselves.
Floating Phonemes orbited around it like satellites.

Currently empty, as she was in The Mouseion on his behalf.

Two thrones fused into one, facing opposite directions yet somehow both facing the Arena.

chapters.title: Chapter 4790: Absolute Denial!
paragraphs: In an area not too far from the Arena.

In a region filled with waves of Paradox and Immensity, the bodies of THE Weavers were floating above an obsidian-gold sea. The liquid below churned with contradictions made manifest, patterns that should have been impossible coexisting in constant flux.
In front of them was a throne of an Absolute.
Paradoxos the Dual sat upon it.
Ortheysat upon it.

The entity defied singular description. Two figures occupied a single space, their forms overlapping and separating in constant rhythm. One face was masculine, carved with sharp features that spoke of cold logic. The other was feminine, softer lines that held warmth that contradicted the coldness of its counterpart. Both faces existed simultaneously, neither dominant, neither subservient.

Their body was half obsidian, half gold, the division line shifting with each breath. Sometimes the left side was dark and the right was bright. Sometimes it reversed. Sometimes both sides were both colors at once.
They wore robes that flowed in two directions simultaneously, fabric that defied the laws of physics by moving with and against gravity in equal measure.
Their eyes were the most unsettling aspect.

Four eyes total, two per face, each one holding depths that seemed to look at everything and nothing. They perceived truth and falsehood as the same thing. They saw possibility and impossibility as interchangeable concepts.
This was Paradoxos the Dual.
Strategos of the Paradoxian Way.
An Absolute bound to THE Agora of Primordial Judgment.
And they were looking toward THE Weavers withdistaste.
Yet THE Weavers remained calm.
All three bodies spoke in unison, their voices layering into something that was one and many simultaneously.
"I can understand the hatred of you four toward us all."
Their golden eyes held no concern for the displeasure being directed at them.
"But you still follow the philosophy of Paradox. The one who claimed it all can forever put you in his service."
Their smiles were identical across three faces.
"Because how can you deny that which you follow?"
The three bodies of THE Weavers spoke as one.

Golden threads moved all around them, countless strings of fate and destiny swirling in patterns that only they could fully perceive. Two of the three bodies held golden scissors, and they were cutting multiple threads all at once. Snip. Snip. Snip. Each cut severed something important somewhere in Existence. Each cut altered the weavings of reality according to their design.
They worked even while conversing.
Even while facing an Absolute who clearly despised them.
Paradoxos looked at THE Weavers with a cold gaze.
Then both mouths opened, and their voice boomed out with weight that made the obsidian-gold sea churn violently.
"We can respect and hate with great intensity."
The words came from two throats as one sound.
"All of us are Absolutes, yet who decided for some of us to be locked while others run free? Who decided that the rest of us had to constantly fight?"
Their four eyes burned with ancient grievance.
"It does not matter either way."
The tone shifted to something more businesslike.
"I have sent a message to THE Living Paradox that his three ugly little weapons have somehow landed in my place."
THE Weavers’ scissors paused momentarily.
"He wanted me to tell you that your other little project, Gilgamesh, is gone."
The words landed with weight.
"You did not manage to protect a good seed, he said. That in itself is a failure."
Paradoxos leaned forward on their contradictory throne.
"And after this, there can be no more. There can be no surprises."
Their voice grew heavier.
"So he asks you... Osmont is not an Absolute, but he is one of THE Four. If you are not confident, step out of the way, and I can take care of it."
The air grew thick with tension.

"Because the glory of THE Four is written in their impossibilities that they perform. Gilgamesh now lies on that wall of impossibility, and THE Living Paradox would much prefer if THE Weavers did not join it."
Both faces smiled without warmth.
"So he asks again. Are you confident?"
BOOM!
The question was a heavy one!

The three Weavers had their golden pupils spin with a sense of insult and glory! How dare anyone question their confidence? How dare THE Living Paradox himself suggest they might not be capable of handling one being who wasn’t even an Absolute?
They were about to reply when Paradoxos continued.
"This was not a question for you to answer."
Their voice cut through the beginning of THE Weavers’ response.
"He has already answered it on your behalf."
Paradoxos waved their hands.
"He has paid a heavy cost to lend you this from me."
HUUM!
The space before THE Weavers began to distort!
Something emerged from the contradiction between existence and non-existence!

It held a blinding obsidian light of Paradox that could barely be observed! The radiance hurt to look at, not because it was bright, but because it shouldn’t have been possible to perceive! It was a thing that existed and didn’t exist, a concept given form that defied the very nature of conceptualization!
It was a collection of multiple Fragments of an Axiom!
And it looked nearly complete!
Paradoxos gestured toward the impossible object.
"An almost complete Axiom."
Their voice held weight that made reality itself pay attention.
"THE Axiom of Absolute Denial."
The name alone made the air grow heavier.
"Its capability is simple, yet it is perhaps the most terrifying of all Axioms that exist, if only it were complete..."
Paradoxos’s four eyes fixed on THE Weavers.
"Whatever the wielder wishes to deny... is denied. Absolutely."
The words were simple.
The implications were not.
"An attack coming toward you? Denied. A Declaration being enacted against you? Denied. The very concept of your defeat? Denied."
Their voice grew colder.
"In its complete form, wielded by an Absolute, it would make the user nigh invincible. Nothing could touch them. Nothing could harm them. Nothing could affect them in any way they did not permit."
The almost complete Axiom pulsed with obsidian light.
"This version is not complete. It has limitations. But against someone who is not an Absolute..."
Paradoxos smiled with both faces.
"It should be more than sufficient."
THE Weavers looked at the almost complete Axiom of Absolute Denial.
All three bodies studied it with golden eyes that spun with calculation and growing excitement.
Then all three smiled eerily.
"Man, now this is just overkill."
Their voices layered into amused acknowledgment.
"Okay."

They reached out, and the almost complete Axiom flowed into their collective existence. It merged with their being, its obsidian light intertwining with the golden threads that perpetually surrounded them.
With such words, THE Weavers looked at Paradoxos.
They stopped cutting the golden strings around them.
"I believe I have been called."
Their smiles held promise of violence to come.
"See you on the other side."
Then, with a flash of brilliance, she disappeared!
The obsidian-gold sea continued to churn in their absence.
Paradoxos remained on their throne, four eyes staring at where THE Weavers had been with contemplation!

chapters.title: Chapter 4791: Making History!
paragraphs: Sometimes, one had to tune out the noise completely.
Regardless of whether there were thousands of entities who had all forged their Civilizations situated across The Palaestra.
Regardless of whether the four Absolutes sat on their thrones or not!
Noah looked at Skoll and finished rubbing his head.
"Alright, go to that hairy old man there and the little fox. Stay with them no matter what, okay?"
He pointed toward the distance where Ul’moreth and Lumivara stood alongside Lunaris and Ophelia and other Glossarians.
Skoll nodded with shining eyes!
He was no longer bound by the power that had kept him in the Substitution Circle. With a flash of neon light, he disappeared and reappeared right between Ul’moreth and Lumivara!
His tail wagged happily as he sat down like a good boy, ready to watch his Master do whatever his Master needed to do.
Noah stood up imperiously.
He looked at the other end of the Arena where at this moment, there was nobody on the other side.
And yet he remained standing.
His body began to billow with flames.

Blue-gold plasmic fire wrapped around his form like a second skin, his toga shining resplendently beneath the radiance. The Phonemes inscribed across his garments blazed brighter. The adornments of his Polemarch status caught light that seemed to come from within him rather than from any external source.
His immense foundations exceeding even THE Creature at this stage began to leak out and spread!
A sense of suffocation radiated from him!
Absolute Immovable Object!

He was an absolute immovable as at this moment, where his feet stood, he would not be moved! The Reckoning Stone beneath him seemed to groan under the weight of his presence. The air compressed around his form. Reality itself acknowledged that something heavy had planted itself in this spot.
And his aura stretched out maddeningly!

Even from afar, a sense of suffocation no Fundamental Depth entity should have radiated from him. Hoplites in the lowest seats felt their breathing grow labored. Lochagoi shifted uncomfortably under the pressure. Even some Polemarchs raised eyebrows at the intensity bleeding off this single being.
The loud noises turned into hushed whispers soon enough.
And Noah continued tuning everything out.
An instant later...
WUU!
The figures of THE Weavers appeared on the other end of the Arena!

Three bodies materialized simultaneously, each one identical to the others. Ancient crones with skin like weathered parchment, eyes of spinning gold that seemed to perceive threads invisible to all others. Their white hair flowed in patterns that defied natural movement. Their fingers were long and spindly, built for the task of cutting and weaving fate itself.
They gazed toward Noah with smiles and malice.

All three bodies even waved at him, casual gestures of greeting as if they were saying hello to a friend they were about to destroy. Their golden scissors gleamed at their sides. Their threads swirled around them in lazy spirals.
The disconnect between their friendly waves and the murderous intent in their eyes was jarring.
Moments after she appeared, three of the four thrones above seemed to have gained immense weight!
But Glossikos’s throne remained empty.
OOOH!
The Voice of Reckoning boomed out across The Palaestra.
"Welcome to The Circle of Reckoning! The Challenger, THE Weavers, Lochagoi of the Paradoxian Way, have arrived!"
The voice carried across every corner of the Arena.

"And though this may seem unfair as it appears to be three against one, the three are actually a single body separated! One existence divided across three forms! This is permitted under the rules of Challenge!"
A dramatic pause.

"And what a Challenge this is! This debate and battle is a grand one that depicts Paradox against The First Tongue in ways that many here do not even comprehend! This is a battle of philosophies that will-"
"Shut the fuck up."
BOOM!
Noah spoke such words calmly!
The Voice of Reckoning cut off instantly!
Immense quietness descended all around as he looked at THE Weavers!
The entire Arena fell silent. Thousands of beings who had been murmuring and shifting went still. The Voice itself, ancient and supposedly unstoppable, simply... stopped.
Because THE Genesis Monarch had told it to.
And in this place, in matters concerning The First Tongue, his authority was not something that could be easily dismissed.
His imperious glare swept across the distance toward his opponents.

Radiant Seals flickered over his skin, the 27 Absolute constructs pulsing with weight that pressed against reality itself. His eyes burned with blue-gold fire. His stance was that of someone who had already decided how this would end.
He didn’t even gaze above to spare a glance at the three Absolutes he hadn’t seen before.
They were irrelevant to this moment.
He kept his gaze on THE Weavers.
"When was the last time that an Absolute fell?"
His voice carried across the silent Arena.
"Do you happen to know?"
BOOM!
The words were heavy!
THE Weavers cackled in response!

All three bodies laughed simultaneously, the sound layering into something that was one voice and many at once. Their smiles widened as terrifying pressure leaked from their bodies. The cheerful wave was replaced by something far more ancient.
Their forms shifted.

The pretense of friendly old women fell away, revealing what truly lay beneath. Decrepit ancient beings whose age transcended normal comprehension. Entities who had existed since The Infinite Unfurling, since before the modern shape of Existence was formed. Their skin grew more weathered. Their eyes burned brighter with golden malevolence. Their fingers elongated into things that looked less like appendages and more like instruments of fate itself.
"Absolutes do not die."
All three voices spoke as one, carrying weight that pressed against Noah’s aura.
"For those who do fall at the hands of other Absolutes..."
Their smiles became something knowing and cruel.
"We respect them enough not to spread stories of their demise. Their endings are private affairs. Their collapses are not entertainment for lesser beings."
"Oh?"
Noah nodded his head at this.
Then he smiled.
"Then it looks like I will be making history today."
His flames blazed brighter.
"Come on now, you decrepit hags. Let’s see what you have up your sleeves."
BOOM!
The words landed like a challenge that could not be taken back!
THE Weavers’ golden eyes spun faster!
The Arena held its breath!

Three bodies materialized simultaneously, each one identical to the others.
Ancient crones with skin like weathered parchment, eyes of spinning gold that seemed to perceive threads invisible to all others.
Their white hair flowed in patterns that defied natural movement.
Their fingers were long and spindly, built for the task of cutting and weaving fate itself.
They gazed toward Noah with smiles and malice.
All three bodies even waved at him, casual gestures of greeting as if they were saying hello to a friend they were about to destroy.
Their golden scissors gleamed at their sides.
Their threads swirled around them in lazy spirals.
The disconnect between their friendly waves and the murderous intent in their eyes was jarring.
Moments after she appeared, three of the four thrones above seemed to have gained immense weight!
But Glossikos’s throne remained empty.
OOOH!
The Voice of Reckoning boomed out across The Palaestra.
"Welcome to The Circle of Reckoning!
The Challenger, THE Weavers, Lochagoi of the Paradoxian Way, have arrived!"
The voice carried across every corner of the Arena.
"And though this may seem unfair as it appears to be three against one, the three are actually a single body separated!
One existence divided across three forms!
This is permitted under the rules of Challenge!"
A dramatic pause.
"And what a Challenge this is!
This debate and battle is a grand one that depicts Paradox against The First Tongue in ways that many here do not even comprehend!
This is a battle of philosophies that will-"
"Shut the fuck up."
BOOM!
Noah spoke such words calmly!
The Voice of Reckoning cut off instantly!
Immense quietness descended all around as he looked at THE Weavers!
The entire Arena fell silent.
Thousands of beings who had been murmuring and shifting went still.
The Voice itself, ancient and supposedly unstoppable, simply... stopped.
Because THE Genesis Monarch had told it to.
And in this place, in matters concerning The First Tongue, his authority was not something that could be easily dismissed.
His imperious glare swept across the distance toward his opponents.
Radiant Seals flickered over his skin, the 27 Absolute constructs pulsing with weight that pressed against reality itself.
His eyes burned with blue-gold fire.
His stance was that of someone who had already decided how this would end.
He didn’t even gaze above to spare a glance at the three Absolutes he hadn’t seen before.
They were irrelevant to this moment.
He kept his gaze on THE Weavers.
"When was the last time that an Absolute fell?"
His voice carried across the silent Arena.
"Do you happen to know?"
BOOM!
The words were heavy!
THE Weavers cackled in response!
All three bodies laughed simultaneously, the sound layering into something that was one voice and many at once.
Their smiles widened as terrifying pressure leaked from their bodies.
The cheerful wave was replaced by something far more ancient.
Their forms shifted.
The pretense of friendly old women fell away, revealing what truly lay beneath.
Decrepit ancient beings whose age transcended normal comprehension.
Entities who had existed since The Infinite Unfurling, since before the modern shape of Existence was formed.
Their skin grew more weathered.
Their eyes burned brighter with golden malevolence.
Their fingers elongated into things that looked less like appendages and more like instruments of fate itself.
"Absolutes do not die."
All three voices spoke as one, carrying weight that pressed against Noah’s aura.
"For those who do fall at the hands of other Absolutes..."
Their smiles became something knowing and cruel.
"We respect them enough not to spread stories of their demise.
Their endings are private affairs.
Their collapses are not entertainment for lesser beings."
"Oh?"
Noah nodded his head at this.
Then he smiled.
"Then it looks like I will be making history today."
His flames blazed brighter.
"Come on now, you decrepit hags.
Let’s see what you have up your sleeves."
BOOM!
The words landed like a challenge that could not be taken back!
THE Weavers’ golden eyes spun faster!
The Arena held its breath!

chapters.title: Chapter 4792: You Could Never Be Me! I
paragraphs: How exactly did one go about collapsing an Absolute that could not be collapsed?
Not even one at that, but three bodies of a single Absolute. Each body still emanated the ridiculous Depth of an Absolute Depth entity.
If you proposed this problem to any other being that did not have the level of an Absolute, they would begin digging their grave and simply wait to walk into it.
Because it was an impossible fucking situation.
And yet...
Noah held this impossible situation and was not digging his grave just yet.
He was not even thinking about utilizing an Anchor Point to activate THE Existential Paradox Loop!

This was a safeguard for his Civilization and Way, but it was not the final solution to everything. If he went across Existence with a mindset that if things were impossible to overcome, there was always the fact that he could reverse time itself... he knew that he would not achieve anything glorious in his journey.
He still treated everything that he did as if there was no safety net.
So even though he was facing an Absolute at this very moment, he did not plan to die and instead would be trying out a daring action.
THE Weavers were at the Lochagoi ranking. Even with whatever help they had received from Paradoxos, they could not raise their Merit as fast as he did with his contributions to The First Tongue.
So they were effectively supposed to be only expressing the aura of an Intermediate Depth entity.
But the sheer Immensity they radiated was enough to crush any Fundamental Depth entities.
An Absolute had to be given their respect.
Normally.
But Noah would not be giving any respect to these three shrewd fuckers.
Now, back to the main point.
The collapse of an Absolute.
His plan was actually a relatively simple one. It may only be capable of working once, maybe multiple times if he did not have an audience. But since he did not have this luxury, he merely acted.
And he...
While everyone watched breathlessly to see what move would be made by the combatants in the Arena...
Noah shockingly took his right hand and plunged it into his chest!
His muscles opened freely as if allowing everything to happen!
Crimson-gold blood leaked out to form swirling rivers around him that shaped themselves into infinity symbols! The blood moved with purpose, painting patterns of boundlessness in the air itself!
And from the hand that he plunged into his chest, he shockingly grasped an incandescent object.
And pulled out... a Heart.
DUM! DUM! DUM!
The beat of the Heart permeated across this entire place!

Every single entity in The Palaestra felt a sense of exhilaration and trepidation wash over them! The sound was not merely auditory. It resonated through their very foundations. It made their own Hearts beat in sympathy. It made their very Ways tremble with recognition of what they were perceiving!
His Heart!
THE Heart of THE Genesis Monarch of Infinite Lexicons!
It was unfathomably glorious!

The size of two fists pressed together, it blazed with blue-gold radiance that made the artificial lighting of The Palaestra seem dim by comparison. Veins of crystallized Mana ran across its surface in patterns that wrote and rewrote themselves constantly. It pulsed with life that transcended mere biological function.
Twirling Archai orbited around it like satellites around a star!
Seals of Absolute Tongue wrapped around it in protective embrace!
This was not merely an organ. This was the concentrated essence of everything Noah had become. His Claim. His Way. His authority over The First Tongue itself.
A moment later, from Noah’s head, a radiant blue-gold book also emerged!
It was none other than THE Grimoire of Infinite Lexicons!
Its pages opened to the halfway point, blank sheets waiting to be filled with compressed foundations. He shockingly took his Heart and placed it upon the pages of the Grimoire.
Its terrifyingly sacred aura erupted immensely in the next moment!
Every single follower of The First Tongue in The Palaestra rose to their feet in shock!
Glossarians gasped!
Hoplites fell to their knees!
Lochagoi stumbled backward!
Polemarchs reached out as if they could grasp what they were seeing from across the Arena!
The empty throne of Glossikos far above was instantly filled!
She appeared with a look of shock that transcended her normally composed demeanor! Her pages rustled violently! Her obsidian-blue eyes widened to impossible degrees!
Moments later, all others rose with utter solemnity!
Paradoxos stood on their contradictory throne, four eyes fixed on what was happening below.
Khaotikos looked over, his expression shifting to something unreadable!
Ontikos... even Ontikos seemed to lean forward slightly, a movement that for him was equivalent to screaming!
Thereafter, Noah took the Grimoire and Heart before him...
And pushed it out calmly.
It floated toward THE Weavers.
All three bodies of THE Weavers had an incredulous look on every single one of their faces.
Noah’s imposing figure stood with an open chest, crimson-gold blood still flowing in infinity patterns around him. His eyes burned with certainty that defied the madness of what he was doing.
"That right there is the entirety of my Way and Claim of The First Tongue."
His voice carried across the silent Arena.
"Many want my Claim. Many want to be one of THE Four."
He gestured toward the floating Grimoire and Heart.
"As an Absolute, you should be able to tell whether it’s genuine. That right there... is everything that many dream of."
His smile held no warmth.
"Take it, and you can effectively claim The First Tongue."
He spread his arms.
"My... Everything."
BOOM!
His singular action was so ridiculous and devastating and unbelievable all at once that even THE Weavers didn’t know how to react!
The Grimoire and the Heart floated toward them rapidly!

Outside the Arena, the figure of Paradoxos stood up and floated above as if they wanted to enter the Arena themselves. Their four eyes fumed with greed that contradicted itself! Two faces twisted with desire that was the same and different simultaneously!

chapters.title: Chapter 4793: You Could Never Be Me! II
paragraphs: The figure of Khaotikos the Unbound floated up and laughed madly!
His voice boomed out like bells of chaos!
"BAHAHA! WHAT IS THIS?! WHAT IS HAPPENING?!"
Ontikos remained still, but his body flared with multicolored flames that had not been there before. The most stable structure in the Arena was experiencing agitation.
And Glossikos...
She looked toward Noah with a gaze as if she had been betrayed!
As if she asked... dude, what the fuck?!

If he was going to give away the Claim of The First Tongue, he was just with her bathing inside pools moments ago! He had contributed 9 new Phonemes! He had gone through all 9 Cycles of Katharsis! He had achieved the distinction of Absolute Immovable Object!
And now he was just... giving it away?!
What was most anger-inducing was the fact that none of them could even interfere in this battle or enter the Arena.
Unless...
Glossikos looked toward Paradoxos.
Paradoxos also turned to look at her.
And the two of them turned to look at the other two Absolutes on their thrones.
If all four of them came to the same decision, they could override the rules of anything in this domain!

Beings at this level communicated extremely fast. Glossikos and Paradoxos communicated with Khaotikos and Ontikos as they got closer and closer to the Arena boundary, asking for all four of them to be in agreement to open it up.
Whoever could get to the Heart first, it was fair game!
And yet...
"Bahaha... where’s the fun in that? NO!"
Khaotikos shockingly denied them!
Glossikos and Paradoxos looked toward him with anger that could have collapsed lesser beings.
They could only whip their heads back to observe.
A radiant book and Heart which represented the very Claim for The First Tongue was floating toward THE Weavers!

Now, with how every single Absolute who could not get their hands on it was reacting, one could understand how THE Weavers felt when they had the very thing that everybody wanted coming straight for them.
Their eyes seemed to pulse with disbelief and incredulity.
They didn’t even need to ascertain whether this was a trick or anything, because as Absolutes, they could feel it!
They could feel that Noah had truly and completely laid out his Claim in that Heart and in that Grimoire!
If they took it...
If they accepted the weight of that Way and Civilization...
They would effectively be holding the Claim to the very First Tongue.
One of THE Four!
THE Four!
OH!
"Mine! Mine!! MINE!"
BOOM!
All three bodies of THE Weavers surged with Immensity!
Their hands outstretched toward the book and the Heart! Even the three of them, which were the same person, were fighting over who could get their hands on it first.
"MINE!"
The joy and euphoria on the faces of THE Weavers was absolute.
Every single one of them grabbed hold of the Grimoire and Heart.
And they sensed it!
Unbelievably, they sensed the Claim to THE First Tongue in their hands!
Even now, as they held it right in their hands, they turned toward Noah at his open chest. He was looking at them calmly.
As if they were looking at him and shaking their heads while asking... what the fuck, man? This is like, really real?!
Thereafter, they only shook their heads as if to say, what a fuckingbuffoonthat guy was!
The euphoria of The First Tongue was just that intense.
Because this effectively meant they would be in the rare company of entities like THE Creature and THE Living Paradox and THE Primordial Chaos!
As they held the Heart and Grimoire, Glossikos outside howled out with agony and valor as if she was seeing her lover taken by another right in front of her eyes.
Paradoxos had an extremely vile expression, both faces twisted with identical fury!
Khaotikos continued to laugh, but even his laughter had taken on an edge.
Ontikos remained still, but the multicolored flames around him blazed brighter.
And in the Arena, THE Weavers roared out...
"THE First Tongue is mine! Mine! I shall take it from the hands of the unworthy! I shall claim... THE First Tongue!"
THE Weavers cackled while saying such words.
Incandescent blue-gold light shone everywhere.
On the other side, Noah watched on with an imperious glare.
THE Weavers began to flicker with an endless light of Mana!
An Infinite light of Mana!
An Infinite light of The First Tongue!
And...
Shockingly, their cackling laughter came to a stop.
Their expressions changed soon after.
And in the next moment...
"KAAAAA!"
An unfathomably piercing screech that could have shattered the Depth of any Fundamental entity boomed out!
The bodies of THE Weavers trembled.
At this moment, all of their golden pupils cracked and became hollow sockets.
"What is this?! WHAT IS THIS?! IT IS TOO MUCH!"
BOOM!
The cracks spread across their bodies in an unfathomable progression!
Shockingly, their very Depth seemed to be collapsing inward in an unfathomable manner!
Noah watched this scene with imperious eyes.
He took a single step and appeared right before THE Weavers.
Right before the storm of billowing brilliance!
He stood inches away from them.

They were holding both his Heart and Grimoire. Their Existence was collapsing in on itself. Every single one of them was trying to pry their hands away from his Heart and Grimoire as if they no longer wanted The First Tongue.
But their fingers would not obey.
The Claim had been accepted.
And now it was consuming them!
Because... what was the only reason Noah was able to lay a Claim on The First Tongue?
What did he have that nobody else held?
Noah’s figure shone with interminable glory as he spoke at this moment.
"You seek to hold and claim The First Tongue."
His voice came cold and absolute.
"But... do you hold any Infinities within you to bear the Infinity of The First Tongue?"
BOOM!
The words were akin to a death sentence!
THE Weavers turned their eyeless sockets to him!
He could see the incredulity, trepidation, and disbelief in their hollow gazes!
At this moment, he did not attack.
He did not even conjure up a single Seal.
Because THE Weavers... were bearing the full weight of THE First Tongue they sought to claim!
And yet they didn’t have any Infinity to back their Claim!
Their very Depth should be getting collapsed by the Immensity of THE First Tongue that permeated across all of Observable Existence.
The First Tongue was not merely a language.
It was the foundational authority of reality itself.
It permeated through every corner of Observable Existence.
It was spoken by countless beings across countless realms.
And the weight of all of that... was now pressing down on THE Weavers.
Without Infinity to bear it.
Without the capability to hold what they had so greedily grasped.
"This... is... impossible..."
Three voices croaked out at once.
Noah looked at them with lividity.
He raised his head imperiously.
"You try to claim what I have when you can’t even express a glimmer of who I am?"
His voice grew heavier.
"You threaten my dog?"
Heavier still.
"You try and kill my people?"
His eyes blazed with blue-gold fury.
"You have THE First Tongue before you, and you can’t even claim it!"
He took a step closer.
"You try to do what I did, when you could never do it!"
His voice became absolute.
"You... COULD NEVER BE ME!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4794: History! I
paragraphs: As he said such terrifying words, an unfathomable Immensity that nobody could sense or see passed down.
It was the weight of all of THE First Tongue across Observable Existence pressing down on an Absolute...
And snuffing out absolutely everything!
Someone had failed their Claim on one of the four aspects of the Oldest Paradox of Existence.
And the penalty for failure... was annihilation.
Before Noah, the bodies of THE Weavers stood still.
No words.
No Immensity.
Nothing.
Even Noah breathed hard as if he couldn’t half believe it had occurred. As if he couldn’t believe it had worked!
He beckoned to his Heart and Grimoire.
They floated back to him.
His Heart reinserted itself into his chest, muscles closing around it as if welcoming it home. His Grimoire sank back into his existence, its pages closing with finality.
And a moment later...
His expression became heavy.
His existence buzzed with pain.
Crimson-gold blood began to leak from his nose and mouth.
|You have taken a dangerous and unprecedented action with your Claim.|
|Allowing another to attempt claiming The First Tongue has caused grievous injury to your Way.|
|Your Claim is too distinguished to be passed around freely.|
|The weight of THE First Tongue pressing down through your offered Claim has damaged the foundations you built.|
|CONSEQUENCE|
|Your comparative Way has fallen from THE Fundamental Depth to THE Intermediate Depth.|
|Your overall Formless Depth has been shaken slightly.|
|Recovery will require time and resources.|
|Your Way and actions have achieved something unfathomably remarkable.|
|An Absolute has fallen.|
|I repeat, an Absolute...has fallen.|
Noah felt breathless.
It had... worked?
An Absolute... had fallen?
The moment such a thing was truly ascertained...
BOOM!
From where THE Weavers floated, cracks appeared in reality itself!
These cracks glowed with obsidian-gold brilliance that shattered Existence itself.
The cracks spread outward from the point of death, spanning across The Palaestra in branching patterns that looked like lightning frozen in space!
From all around, Hoplites scrambled away from the spreading fractures.
Lochagoi fled toward the edges of the Arena.
Polemarchs erected barriers to protect themselves and those near them.
The Reckoning Stone beneath the point of collapse began to crumble!
The Four Pillars trembled!
The Nexus of Truth blazed with light it had never shown before.
Glossikos and the other Absolutes... stood where they were with a myriad of expressions and incredulity.
Glossikos looked at Noah with something that transcended shock. Her figurr had gone completely still.
Paradoxos wore expressions of fury and disbelief on both faces simultaneously.
Khaotikos had stopped laughing entirely, his features frozen in something that might have been awe.
Ontikos... for the first time in recorded history, Ontikos moved. He leaned forward on his throne of uncarved marble.
As such a terrifying thing occurred, the region where THE Weavers stood collapsed entirely!
It became a terrifying vacuum!
The bodies of THE Weavers disappeared into the void created through their failure!
Nothing remained where they had been!
Only an absence!
Only a wound in reality where something that should have existed no longer did!
|You have triggered the first death of an Absolute across Observable Existence after THE Fallout.|
|What... have you done?|
|An Unknown and Unfathomable process is beginning as a connection with something Absolute has been established.|
|THE Absolute Everythings that made up THE Absolute you collapsed are yours to claim:|
|- Their Weavings (the accumulated threads of fate they had cut and woven)|
|- Their Bodies, Their Depths (the authority they had gathered across eons)|
|- All Items on their Existence at the time of collapse|
|This includes: THE Axiom of Absolute Denial (almost complete), Fragments of Axioms|
|This includes: The Golden Scissors of Fate (three sets)|
|This includes: Accumulated threads representing countless severed destinies|
|WARNING|
|Due to the collapse of an Absolute, unknown changes are unraveling.|
|Reality is adjusting to accommodate the absence|
|Error.|
|Information procurement and analysis is temporarily being hindered. Hold on.|
BOOM!
Noah stood at the edge of the vacuum that had once been THE Weavers.
Blood continued to leak from his nose and mouth.
What truly happened when an Absolute died?
It was such a rare and impossible thing.
At this moment, at the point where the vacuum bloomed where THE Weavers used to be...
BOOM!
The vacuum collapsed in on itself again and again.

The cycle repeated with increasing intensity, reality itself unable to process what had just occurred! The absence where an Absolute had existed moments before was too profound for normal space to accommodate! It was not merely empty. It truly and unimaginably was the negation of fullness. The opposite of presence. A wound in Existence that refused to heal.
The entire scene felt tense and sacred.
As if something sacred had fallen.
As if reality itself was holding its breath, uncertain how to proceed.
And at such a moment...
An obsidian-gold pillar of Paradox instantly shot up and down.

It pierced through the ceiling of The Palaestra, through the artificial sky, through barriers that should have been impenetrable! It drove downward through the Reckoning Stone, through the foundations of the Arena, through layers of reality that descended beyond normal perception.
Other pillars of Paradox shot out in all other ordinal directions.

North and south! East and west! And diagonal trajectories that shouldn’t have existed in normal space! The pillars spread outward like the death throes of something fundamental, announcing to all of Observable Existence that one of its Absolutes had ceased to be.
Noah observed all this while his body floated gloriously and illustriously.
His chest had sealed. His Heart and Grimoire had returned to their proper places. But blood still leaked from his nose and mouth, evidence of the price he had paid for this victory.
|INFORMATION EXTRACTION CONTINUING|
|Processing with some difficulty due to unprecedented nature of event.|
|Additional information has been obtained.|
|An Absolute’s Depth is not only contained within their body like lesser beings.|
|It has permeated into Observable Existence itself through eons of existence.|
|THE Weavers existed since before THE Fallout.|
|Their authority had woven itself into the fabric of reality across countless weavings of Existence, and all of this has been collapsed.|
|DEATH CONSEQUENCE|
|When an Absolute dies, this Depth begins to hemorrhage back out of Existence.|
|All Absolutes across Observable Existence will sense the hemorrhaging Depth of another Absolute.|
|They will know what has occurred.|
|The Depth that is hemorrhaging will go toward...!|
|WATCH OUT!|
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4795: History! II
paragraphs: The words of Ruination in the form of prompts only arrived as a blinding pillar of obsidian-gold light shot forth from the vacuum!
It smashed into Noah with force that would have obliterated anything less than what he had become!
But since he was an Absolute Immovable Object, he was not moved back.
He took the impact with a changing expression.
An unbelievably dense concentration of Civilizational Authority flowed toward him.
It was... Absolute Civilizational Authority! The accumulated power of an entity that had existed since before THE Fallout, compressed and channeled directly into his existence.
But it was so unfathomably heavy and painful that he almost felt like he would unravel!

His foundations, already damaged from offering his Claim, groaned under the additional weight before they ate everything and began to recover in an unfathomable way, basked and seeking to integrate what wss coming in.
His Seals of Absolute Tongue blazed with desperate intensity as they tried to process the incoming Depth!
His very Way trembled as authority that belonged to Paradox attempted to merge with authority that belonged to The First Tongue!
But...
|Your Formless Depth withstands against the Immensity of THE Absolute Depth of Absolute Sovereignty flowing into your Existence.|
|You are the entity who caused the causal collapse of an Absolute.|
|By the weavings of Existence, you inherit...most of what they held.|
|By the nature of your Formless classification, you can bear what others could not.|
|Integration proceeding.|
|Integration painful.|
|Due to the collapse of an Absolute, something unique has began to permeate across Observable Existence.|
|THE SILENCE|
|For a brief moment, everything stops.|
|All conflict pauses.|
|All noise ceases.|
|Existence itself seems to mourn, or celebrate.|
|The passing of an Absolute is acknowledged by all aspects of reality.|
Noah felt his Immensity burning and surging up!
But more than this, Existence seemed to truly be mourning.
When he looked around, he felt threads of Paradox mourning.

They wept in ways that transcended normal emotion. The obsidian-gold Weavings that permeated Observable Existence trembled with loss. One of their own had fallen. One who had served THE Living Paradox since before THE Fallout. One who had cut and woven countless destinies.
Gone.
He felt threads of Chaos mourning and buzzing with excitement simultaneously.
The contradiction was pure Chaos. Sorrow and joy coexisting. Loss and gain indistinguishable. Khaotikos’s domain recognized both the tragedy and the opportunity in equal measure.
And surrounding Weavings of Existence and The First Tongue... mourning!
Even his own Claim grieved for what had been lost!
Why?
Why would they be mourning the death of an Absolute?!
THE Weavers had been an enemy! They had hunted him! They had threatened his people! They had targeted his dog!
And yet reality itself wept for their passing!
Noah’s gaze was one of immense glory and Tyranny as if he wanted to rebuke the very aspects of the Oldest Paradox of Existence!
How dare they mourn his enemy?
How dare Existence grieve for those who sought to destroy him?
But he stood there, beginning to accept the rewards and, apparently, the consequences of killing an Absolute.
What he was receiving now seemed to only be the tip of the iceberg.
Since prior to this, he had seen the prompts that detailed the bodies of THE Weavers and everything they held. Which apparently included an Axiom that was almost complete among other things.
All his to claim.
So he stood in what used to be an Arena.
And yet, right now, it was an immense vacuum caused by the collapse of an Absolute. The void continued to collapse in on itself while pillars of incandescent waves of Paradox radiated all around.

The seats that had held thousands of observers were shattered or displaced. The Four Pillars that had stood at compass points around The Circle of Reckoning were cracked and leaning. The Reckoning Stone itself had fractured into countless pieces that floated in the altered gravity around the vacuum.
Around the destroyed Palaestra, four Absolutes gazed toward him with grave eyes.
Eyes as if they were all looking at... an enemy!
As if none of them had truly believed the collapse of an Absolute here was possible.

Glossikos floated near her empty throne, her eyes completely still. Whatever she had found in THE Mouseion of Fated Artifacts remained unknown, as she had returned the moment she sensed what was happening. Her obsidian-blue eyes held something between awe and immensity.

Paradoxos stood on the edge of the destruction, both faces twisted with identical fury. Their four eyes burned with hatred that transcended their normal contradictions. One of THEIR Absolutes had been killed. One who followed THEIR philosophy. And the one who had done it stood before them, covered in blood but very much alive.
Khaotikos’s laughter had stopped.
But one could see his eyes trembling with veiled excitement and wonder.
"The first Absolute to fall was from Paradox."
His voice echoed out across the ruined Arena.
"And the first one to kill an Absolute was not any of the oldest Four..."
His grin returned, but it held edges that cut.
"But the youngest and weakest of THE Four!"
He laughed, but it was not the carefree chaos of before.
"Haha... haha!"
His menacing words echoed out as something far too immense had occurred here.
At this time, Paradoxos stood up grandly.
Their visage emanated waves of menace as they looked toward Noah! The contradiction of their dual nature seemed to have resolved into a singular purpose. Hatred. Pure and undiluted.
Glossikos had her chest rising up and down as if she was on the cusp of making a truly grand decision.

Her eyes flickered between Noah and the vacuum where THE Weavers had been. Between the one who had given her hope for reclaiming what she never had, and the evidence of what that one was capable of doing to Absolutes.
And Ontikos... well, he was particularly unique.
The multicolored glow and flames of Existence around him took on an even heavier intensity. The glow focused on his eyes. They became glazed over as if... as if another was looking through them.
And through that gaze alone, it seemed like a Depth that was more than ten times as grand, if not unfathomably more, was looking at Noah.
Observing THE Genesis Monarch standing amidst the ruins of an Arena, covered in his own blood, surrounded by the hemorrhaging Depth of a dead Absolute.
The death of an Absolute was already an impossibility.
The one who collapsed that Absolute was even more of an impossibility.
It was a single action.
But its effects only just began!

chapters.title: Chapter 4796: THE Youngest Moves First I
paragraphs: Observable Existence was unfathomably vast.
So vast that one could say the only entities who could truly understand the scope of its vastness had to be entities that had attained THE Absolute Depth.
But in the vastness of Existence, far from the Corrupted Vault of Ginnungagap or the endless Weavings of The Wastes of THE Fallout...
In a Primordial Realm known as Alfheimr.
Primordial Realms of Existence were each different. No single one was the same as the other. Some could argue that some realms were lesser, while others were grander.
For anyone making such an argument, Alfheimr... could be considered one of the places that sat at the very top.
At this moment.

The realm stretched out in wonders of impossible beauty. Forests of crystalline trees rose toward skies that shifted between aurora and starlight. Rivers of liquid radiance flowed through valleys carved from solidified dreams. Mountains of pure condensed Mana pierced through clouds that sang when the wind passed through them.
Everything here was more!
More vibrant, ore alive, nore real than reality had any right to be.
In a region where the crystalline forests gave way to meadows of luminescent grass, three figures moved across serenely.

THE Primordial Chaos walked with the casual ease of someone who owned everything and nothing simultaneously. His form shifted constantly, never maintaining the same appearance for more than a few moments.
One instant he was tall and imposing, the next compact and dense. His features rearranged themselves according to no discernible pattern.
THE Living Emotive floated beside him, her body crackling with emotions that changed faster than expressions could form.

THE Living Elemental trailed behind them, his form shrouded by the Phonemes of Fire, Air, Earth, and Water. The four fundamental concepts swirled around him in constant rotation, each one manifesting in brilliant displays.
He moved with the caution of someone who knew he was in the presence of beings far more powerful than himself.
And yet a moment later, their gazes were those of astonishment!
They looked up and saw the illusion of an endlessly blinding pillar of obsidian-gold light shooting across Alfheimr itself!
It wasn’t physically present.
It was a sign.
A signal that permeated across Observable Existence.

Now, the vision of Absolutes was unique. They directly knew what the pillar that they saw meant. Due to their status, they were even able to understand and read what this pillar meant in ways that others could never imagine.
After all, this was a signal that permeated across Observable Existence, but for the most part, it was mainly Absolutes who would gaze upon it and understand exactly what it meant.
And they had not expected to see something like this so soon.
It meant the collapse of another Absolute!
"This is the signature of THE Weavers!"
THE Living Emotive’s voice came out in a shriek of disbelief and excitement.
"THE fucking Weavers! What happened?!"
Her eyes shone with an ecstatic and crazy light as if seeing such a thing gave her a thrilling high!
"Did THE Creature go scorched Existence?!"
She was genuinely shocked!
Even though THE Weavers were what could be considered entities from her camp. Since she also moved alongside THE Living Paradox and THE Loom.
Even though at this very moment, she was standing beside THE Primordial Chaos.
But this woman seemed to have absolutely no allegiances.
At this moment, both her and Elemental looked deeply into this pillar that represented the collapse of an Absolute. It communicated many things for those who could perceive them.
Right now they knew the identity of who had been collapsed.
And they were reading the sign that permeated across Observable Existence to seek out... who had done the collapsing.
But before they could fully arrive at an answer...
THE Primordial Chaos frowned.
His grand and magisterial figure billowed with waves of disorder as he spoke calmly.
"It is not THE Creature. He would not kill."
His voice held certainty that transcended normal perception.
"It is... THE Youngest."
BOOM!
Chaos did not even need to look at the dazzling sign above to find out information on exactly what had happened.
He simply knew.
"THE Youngest? Who the fuck is the youngest?"
Emotive’s expression shifted through confusion and dawning realization.
"Wait... you don’t mean..."
She was astonished!
She wanted to see it for herself!
Focusing on the Sign above, she poured her perception into reading its message. Moments later, a barely imperceptible image formed within the obsidian-gold light.
An image of... Osmont!
It looked grand. Immovable. Standing imperiously in a toga, surrounded by blue gold flames!
But it was there.
Emotive and Elemental were shocked to confirm it!
Osmont!
Osmont?!
That fucker wasn’t even at THE Surface Depth before THE Fallout, right?!
THE Living Elemental had sent him a savage curse of burning from THE Loom. At that time, Osmont was not at THE.
He had been nothing!
A speck!
An ant that Elemental had tried to crush.
And now...
"Haha... no fucking way, right?"
THE Living Emotive’s body shone with a manic light of countless emotions!
"The weakest of THE Four is the first one who made a move to kill an Absolute?!"
Her laughter echoed across the luminescent meadows of Alfheimr.
"And not just any Absolute, but THE Weavers?! I mean, I know they’re a bit shit since they fully rely on Paradox, but still... damn!"
Her emotions cycled faster and faster as she processed the implications!
And then her expression shone as if she gained a new understanding.
She looked toward THE Living Elemental.
Who had an absolutely ashen expression.
A brutal and somewhat heavy scene unfolded as THE Living Emotive pointed at him while she laughed with mania!
"Haha, Elemental, you’re absolutely fucked!"
Her finger jabbed toward him accusingly.
"Did you not curse the youngest before he even became THE?! He must fucking hate you!"
Her laughter grew more unhinged.
"And you... you are not stronger than THE Weavers, are you? Maybe about the same?"
She tilted her head with mock concern.
"Woah woah woah... this means your existence is on a timer!"
Her grin became something feral.
"That... is fucking hilarious!"

In a Primordial Realm known as Alfheimr.
Primordial Realms of Existence were each different.
No single one was the same as the other.
Some could argue that some realms were lesser, while others were grander.
For anyone making such an argument, Alfheimr... could be considered one of the places that sat at the very top.
At this moment.
The realm stretched out in wonders of impossible beauty.
Forests of crystalline trees rose toward skies that shifted between aurora and starlight.
Rivers of liquid radiance flowed through valleys carved from solidified dreams.
Mountains of pure condensed Mana pierced through clouds that sang when the wind passed through them.
Everything here was more!
More vibrant, ore alive, nore real than reality had any right to be.
In a region where the crystalline forests gave way to meadows of luminescent grass, three figures moved across serenely.
THE Primordial Chaos walked with the casual ease of someone who owned everything and nothing simultaneously.
His form shifted constantly, never maintaining the same appearance for more than a few moments.
One instant he was tall and imposing, the next compact and dense.
His features rearranged themselves according to no discernible pattern.
THE Living Emotive floated beside him, her body crackling with emotions that changed faster than expressions could form.
THE Living Elemental trailed behind them, his form shrouded by the Phonemes of Fire, Air, Earth, and Water.
The four fundamental concepts swirled around him in constant rotation, each one manifesting in brilliant displays.
He moved with the caution of someone who knew he was in the presence of beings far more powerful than himself.
And yet a moment later, their gazes were those of astonishment!
They looked up and saw the illusion of an endlessly blinding pillar of obsidian-gold light shooting across Alfheimr itself!
It wasn’t physically present.
It was a sign.
A signal that permeated across Observable Existence.
Now, the vision of Absolutes was unique.
They directly knew what the pillar that they saw meant.
Due to their status, they were even able to understand and read what this pillar meant in ways that others could never imagine.
After all, this was a signal that permeated across Observable Existence, but for the most part, it was mainly Absolutes who would gaze upon it and understand exactly what it meant.
And they had not expected to see something like this so soon.
It meant the collapse of another Absolute!
"This is the signature of THE Weavers!"
THE Living Emotive’s voice came out in a shriek of disbelief and excitement.
"THE fucking Weavers!
What happened?!"
Her eyes shone with an ecstatic and crazy light as if seeing such a thing gave her a thrilling high!
"Did THE Creature go scorched Existence?!"
She was genuinely shocked!
Even though THE Weavers were what could be considered entities from her camp.
Since she also moved alongside THE Living Paradox and THE Loom.
Even though at this very moment, she was standing beside THE Primordial Chaos.
But this woman seemed to have absolutely no allegiances.
At this moment, both her and Elemental looked deeply into this pillar that represented the collapse of an Absolute.
It communicated many things for those who could perceive them.
Right now they knew the identity of who had been collapsed.
And they were reading the sign that permeated across Observable Existence to seek out... who had done the collapsing.
But before they could fully arrive at an answer...
THE Primordial Chaos frowned.
His grand and magisterial figure billowed with waves of disorder as he spoke calmly.
"It is not THE Creature.
He would not kill."
His voice held certainty that transcended normal perception.
"It is...
THE Youngest."
BOOM!
Chaos did not even need to look at the dazzling sign above to find out information on exactly what had happened.
He simply knew.
"THE Youngest?
Who the fuck is the youngest?"
Emotive’s expression shifted through confusion and dawning realization.
"Wait... you don’t mean..."
She was astonished!
She wanted to see it for herself!
Focusing on the Sign above, she poured her perception into reading its message.
Moments later, a barely imperceptible image formed within the obsidian-gold light.
An image of...
Osmont!
It looked grand.
Immovable.
Standing imperiously in a toga, surrounded by blue gold flames!
But it was there.
Emotive and Elemental were shocked to confirm it!
Osmont!
Osmont?!
That fucker wasn’t even at THE Surface Depth before THE Fallout, right?!
THE Living Elemental had sent him a savage curse of burning from THE Loom.
At that time, Osmont was not at THE.
He had been nothing!
A speck!
An ant that Elemental had tried to crush.
And now...
"Haha... no fucking way, right?"
THE Living Emotive’s body shone with a manic light of countless emotions!
"The weakest of THE Four is the first one who made a move to kill an Absolute?!"
Her laughter echoed across the luminescent meadows of Alfheimr.
"And not just any Absolute, but THE Weavers?!
I mean, I know they’re a bit shit since they fully rely on Paradox, but still... damn!"
Her emotions cycled faster and faster as she processed the implications!
And then her expression shone as if she gained a new understanding.
She looked toward THE Living Elemental.
Who had an absolutely ashen expression.
A brutal and somewhat heavy scene unfolded as THE Living Emotive pointed at him while she laughed with mania!
"Haha, Elemental, you’re absolutely fucked!"
Her finger jabbed toward him accusingly.
"Did you not curse the youngest before he even became THE?!
He must fucking hate you!"
Her laughter grew more unhinged.
"And you... you are not stronger than THE Weavers, are you?
Maybe about the same?"
She tilted her head with mock concern.
"Woah woah woah... this means your existence is on a timer!"
Her grin became something feral.
"That... is fucking hilarious!"

chapters.title: Chapter 4797: THE Youngest Moves First II
paragraphs: THE Living Emotive said such terrifying words.
THE Living Elemental looked at her with icy and flaming eyes simultaneously.
But he did not respond.
Because what could he say?
This entire time, the calm figure of THE Primordial Chaos looked between the two of them as if he was watching children bickering.
"THE Youngest killed that tiny Absolute..."
His voice came measured and thoughtful.
"Before they grasped Absolute themselves."
He paused.
"But when it comes to whether he has the capability to collapse any Absolutes similar to the little Weavers..."
His shifting features settled into something resembling certainty.
"He is not there yet."
These words were heavy!
THE Living Emotive instantly turned toward THE Primordial Chaos.

Her body slid up behind him, arms wrapping around his massive form in an embrace that should have been impossible given their size difference. She whispered in his ear with the intimacy of a conspirator sharing secrets.
"Big guy, what did you find out? Can you share with us?"
Her voice dripped with curiosity and hunger for information.
THE Primordial Chaos was unbothered by the actions of THE Living Emotive.
He simply waved his hands.
And in the next moment, a massive illusory screen appeared above them.
It played out events that had occurred in a distant Palaestra within THE Agora of Primordial Judgment.
It showed THE Weavers and Osmont.
It showed Osmont... presenting them with a beating Heart!
The scene played out in perfect clarity. THE Weavers grasping for the Grimoire and Heart. Their euphoria. Their screams. Their collapse.
THE Primordial Chaos’s expression billowed with endless obsidian Weavings of Chaos as he spoke.
"If you do not want to face an early collapse from the hands of THE Youngest... just leave his Heart alone for now."
His voice held warning.
"He was able to grasp The First Tongue for a reason."
His shifting features darkened.
"THE Weavers did not have that reason. And they tried to do the same."
Contempt entered his tone.
"They read countless fates. And yet they were foolish enough not to know what would happen?"
He shook his head.
"It is a waste for any Absolute to fall, but..."
A glorious and grand expression flashed across the eyes of THE Primordial Chaos!
"Chaos is rising now and gaining an edge. While this entire time, Paradox and Existence have been seeking supremacy."
His smile became something vast and terrible.
"With the collapse of the first Absolute... hmmm."
He hummed to himself with satisfaction that made the air around them vibrate with disorder.
Emotive and Elemental could not take their eyes away from the events playing out on the illusory screen!
At this same time, and even actually in the same place.
In a different region of Alfheimr.

A serene area of radiant waterfalls cascaded from floating islands that hung gloriously in the air. The islands themselves were composed of crystallized Mana so pure that they glowed with soft inner light.
Waterfalls caught the aurora light of Alfheimr’s ever-shifting sky, refracting into countless colors that painted the mist with rainbows that never faded.
On one waterfall, the figure of THE Living Origin sat.
She played with the water as if she was playing with something from home.
And it was home to her.
She and THE First Hunger had just arrived in Alfheimr!

The journey through The Wastes of THE Fallout had been harrowing, but Origin knew paths through the chaos that others did not. She had walked these routes long before THE Fallout had transformed them into nightmares.
Tor stood behind her and watched her back calmly.

His crimson-obsidian eyes observed her as she played with the water and enjoyed being back home after so long. His expression was unreadable, but there was something in the way he positioned himself that was a bit...protective!
THE Living Origin raised her gaze at this moment.

She turned to look at Tor, her hair and eyes shining with gorgeous white-gold radiance. The Origin within her seemed to resonate with Alfheimr itself, as if this realm recognized one of its oldest daughters.
She began speaking to him with a somewhat difficult expression.
"I can’t..."
Before she could say the rest of her words, she looked up in shock!
Tor looked up alongside her!
They saw the pillar of obsidian-gold light tearing across the skies of Alfheimr!
Origin was astonished.
Tor was confused.
He tilted his head and said with genuine uncertainty in his voice.
"What is that?"
Origin had a grave expression as she replied.
"That is the sign of collapse of an Absolute."
Her voice carried weight that made the water around her grow still.
"I wonder which one of those monsters has made the move..."
Monsters.
She was thinking along the lines of either THE Living Paradox or THE Primordial Chaos, or even potentially THE Creature!
She was not an Absolute, so she was not able to fully read that sign. But she had seen a sight like that before. Long ago. In ages that most had forgotten!
She could recognize it.
She wondered.
Just which monstrous thing collapsed an Absolute?
Far from Alfheimr.
In a completely different Primordial Realm with its own musings of Existence.
Within... Jotunheim!

The realm stretched out in wonders of brutal grandeur. Mountains of black ice rose toward skies that crackled with perpetual lightning. Glaciers the size of continents groaned as they shifted across landscapes carved by violence that predated memory.
And across these frozen wastelands, the gloriousChaos Giants of Existencemoved!

Beings of impossible scale, their forms composed of elemental fury given flesh. Some stood hundreds of meters tall, their footsteps causing earthquakes that reshaped the terrain. Others were smaller, merely the size of mountains, but no less fearsome.
Their skin was the color of storms and obsidian. Their eyes burned with the light of dying folds. They were chaos incarnate, descendants of forces that had existed since before differentiation.
Most of them were Pre-THE entities, powerful but not having crossed the threshold into true Depth classification.
But there were also a few hundred entities who had formed their Depth here.
Sitting at THE Surface and Intermediate Depths and Fundamental Depths!
They were the elite of Jotunheim’s Chaos Giants!
